planting.note: Root stem cuttings in chunky, well-drained aroid mix and place within a few feet of an east- or west-facing window; give a moss pole or trellis to climb as fenestrations develop.

directions: Bulbasaur is a collector's selection of the common Swiss cheese plant named for its blotchy, camouflage-like patches of cream, white, and light green scattered irregularly across each deep-green leaf, with no two leaves variegated alike. Keep it within a couple feet of a bright east- or west-facing window, since low light slows growth and mutes the patterning; avoid direct midday sun, which can scorch the thinner white sections. Let the top quarter to half of the potting mix dry before watering again, and provide a pole or trellis so leaves size up and fenestrate as the plant matures.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in chunky, well-drained aroid mix; place within a couple feet of a bright east- or west-facing window and provide a sturdy pole as it climbs toward its mature size of 6 feet or more.

directions: White Monster is a high-contrast Monstera deliciosa selection whose new leaves emerge nearly pure white before settling into dark green marked with bold white variegation, giving it a ghostly look in young growth that mellows with age. It needs notably brighter light than a plain green Monstera to hold its white sectors without reverting, so keep it within a couple feet of an unobstructed window or under supplemental grow lights. Water when the top two inches of mix are dry, provide above-average humidity, and furnish a sturdy climbing support so the large, fenestrated leaves can size up as the plant matures into a floor specimen.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in a chunky, fast-draining aroid mix near an east-facing window; provide a pole or plank for the vining stems to climb as leaves narrow and fenestrate with age.

directions: Unlike the broad-leaved common Monstera deliciosa, this Mayuna-group selection carries narrow, elongated leaves splashed with creamy white, sage, and light green variegation, giving it a more delicate, lace-like silhouette while still developing the fenestrations collectors prize. Place it within a couple feet of an unobstructed east-facing window, or farther from a west-facing one, since variegation fades and growth stalls in dim corners. Let the top quarter to half of the potting mix dry between waterings and give it a moss pole or trellis to climb, which encourages larger, more deeply fenestrated leaves over time.

planting.note: Root stem cuttings in well-drained, humus-rich mix and place near a bright east- or west-facing window; trails neatly from a hanging basket or climbs a small trellis.

directions: Mini Mint is a newer, small-leaved Epipremnum selection with pointed foliage speckled in golden yellow over a minty green base, giving it a finer, denser texture than standard golden pothos. It tolerates medium to lower light without dying back, but the yellow speckling is most vivid within a couple feet of an unobstructed east- or west-facing window. Let the top two inches of potting mix dry before watering again, and train it up a small pole or let it trail from a hanging basket, where it can reach six feet or more over time.

common_name: Dark Hookeri Anthurium (Bird's Nest Anthurium, Dark Form)

planting.note: Grow as a houseplant or shaded patio container in humus-rich, well-drained potting mix; this darker-leaved hookeri selection tolerates average home humidity and infrequent watering better than most collector anthuriums.

directions: This selection of the bird's-nest anthurium carries noticeably deeper green, leathery, paddle-shaped leaves than typical Anthurium hookeri, radiating outward from a central rosette into a full, rounded form prized for foliage rather than flowers. It tolerates medium, indirect light near an east- or west-facing window and even brief morning sun before 10 a.m., but harsh afternoon sun will scorch the leaves. Let the top couple inches of potting mix dry before watering again -- this species shrugs off missed waterings far better than most anthuriums -- and give it warm temperatures with above-average humidity and good air movement for best leaf form.

planting.note: Grow in a wide, shallow container of chunky, well-aerated aroid mix; this dwarf gloriosum crawls horizontally on a rhizome rather than climbing, so allow room to spread sideways rather than upward.

directions: Tinker Bell is a compact selection of the velvet-leaved Philodendron gloriosum, keeping the same heart-shaped, matte-green leaves with contrasting silvery-white veins but at a fraction of the size of standard gloriosum, making it practical for a shelf or small terrarium. Give it bright, indirect light within a couple feet of an east- or west-facing window; it tolerates medium light but grows slower and less vigorously without it. Let the top two inches of mix dry between waterings and keep it warm and humid, since like other gloriosum forms it is a creeping, rhizomatous plant that spreads across the soil surface instead of climbing.

planting.note: Grow as a self-heading houseplant in well-drained, humus-rich potting mix; needs no stake or climbing support, forming a dense upright crown over time.

directions: This variegated sport of the upright Green Congo philodendron produces broad, glossy, self-heading foliage splashed with creamy white, mint, and light green, with new leaves emerging palest before settling into their mature pattern. Keep it in bright indirect light within a couple feet of a window to hold strong variegation and promote larger leaves, allowing brief gentle morning sun but avoiding exposure after mid-morning. Water when the top two inches of soil dry out, feed during the growing season, and expect a sturdy, non-climbing crown reaching 3 to 4 feet tall and wide at maturity.
